actualFailure.domLimit: The Testing Library DOM dump is truncated within the sidebar. It does not show the optional-panel loading fallback and cannot prove that loading or a retry error was visible.
actualFailure.sourceObservation: SettingsOnDemand uses a real dynamic import and caches successful modules. The failed test starts a normal Testing Library findByRole immediately after opening the fallback dialog. Installed @testing-library/dom 10.4.2 defaults asyncUtilTimeout to 1000 ms; this test has no override. Vitest test/hook timeout is 15000 ms with four workers. This was a missing-element query timeout, not the 15-second test timeout.
actualFailure.rootCause: The test combined cold asynchronous Settings module/dependency readiness with the default one-second DOM query deadline. A controlled gate around the real module confirms the old query fails before the import completes, while releasing that gate exposes the actual control and permits all original access-expiry/renewal/draft/unknown/no-replay assertions to pass. The hosted trace does not record the exact import duration, so the controlled ordering is not represented as a replay of its unrecorded scheduling.

whyEarlierChecksMissed: Matrix1 already exposed this same test using a synchronous getByRole before the lazily imported Settings mounted. That repair changed the test to await the actual navigation control and retained all expiry/draft/unknown/no-replay assertions; it did not establish an explicit module-readiness prerequisite.

The subsequent targeted set DID include this actual App-level test, deferred-panel, draft-navigation and other consumers: nine files, 128 identical cases on Windows and Linux all passed. It would be inaccurate to say the failing case was omitted from targeted tests.

The local fourth full matrix also passed this case on Windows and Linux at the same source digest. Those observed successes do not prove a fixed one-second DOM query deadline bounds cold module transformation/import under a different hosted workload. The downloaded logs do not measure the exact import duration or prove a machine-specific slowdown cause.

The generic deferred-panel tests exercise supplied loader promises and retry/unmount behavior, but do not load the actual Settings module dependency graph. Actual App consumers used real imports without deliberately controlling the not-yet-ready boundary. A controlled real-import dependency is required to separate module preparation from the lifecycle behavior being asserted.

Earlier audits reviewed the switch from synchronous lookup to semantic readiness as sufficient and did not challenge the remaining coupling of a DOM-query deadline to a cold bundler/module import. The repeat failure is retained as an incomplete prior prevention rule, not hidden by a green rerun.
